label: 1. Good PR: fix crash on empty input (with tests)
title: Fix IndexError when parse_date receives an empty string
body:
## What
parse_date("") raised an IndexError instead of the documented ValueError.

## Why
Issue #14. Callers can't catch the documented exception type.

## How
Added an early check for empty/whitespace input that raises ValueError with a clear message.

## Tests
Added two tests (empty string, whitespace only). All existing tests pass locally.
contributing:
# Contributing to tinydate
- One focused change per PR.
- Bug fixes must include a test.
- Describe what and why in the PR description.
- Run `pytest` before opening the PR.
diff:
diff --git a/tinydate/parser.py b/tinydate/parser.py
--- a/tinydate/parser.py
+++ b/tinydate/parser.py
@@ -10,6 +10,9 @@ def parse_date(text):
     """Parse YYYY-MM-DD into a date. Raises ValueError on bad input."""
+    if not text or not text.strip():
+        raise ValueError("parse_date() needs a non-empty date string")
     parts = text.strip().split("-")
     year, month, day = int(parts[0]), int(parts[1]), int(parts[2])
     return date(year, month, day)
diff --git a/tests/test_parser.py b/tests/test_parser.py
--- a/tests/test_parser.py
+++ b/tests/test_parser.py
@@ -20,3 +20,11 @@ def test_valid_date():
     assert parse_date("2024-02-29") == date(2024, 2, 29)
+
+def test_empty_string_raises_value_error():
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
+        parse_date("")
+
+def test_whitespace_only_raises_value_error():
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
+        parse_date("   ")

label: 4. Ambiguous: big refactor mixed with a behaviour change
title: Cleanup parser
body: Refactored the parser to be cleaner. Should be mostly the same.
contributing:
# Contributing to tinydate
- One focused change per PR.
- Bug fixes must include a test.
- Describe what and why in the PR description.
diff:
diff --git a/tinydate/parser.py b/tinydate/parser.py
--- a/tinydate/parser.py
+++ b/tinydate/parser.py
@@ -1,40 +1,52 @@
-def parse_date(text):
-    parts = text.strip().split("-")
-    year, month, day = int(parts[0]), int(parts[1]), int(parts[2])
-    return date(year, month, day)
+def _split(text):
+    return [p for p in re.split(r"[-./ ]", text.strip()) if p]
+
+def _to_ints(parts):
+    return [int(p) for p in parts]
+
+def parse_date(text, default=None):
+    try:
+        y, m, d = _to_ints(_split(text))[:3]
+        return date(y, m, d)
+    except Exception:
+        return default
@@ -60,6 +72,6 @@ def format_date(d):
-def validate(text):
-    parse_date(text)
-    return True
+def validate(text):
+    return parse_date(text) is not None
